title: Fast and reliable machine learning-based detection of postoperative intracranial infections in brain tumor patients: a diagnostic study using routine CSF parameters.
summary: Random-forest feature selection and comparison of eleven machine-learning models identified CSF neutrophil percentage, glucose and color as predictors of postoperative intracranial infection; retrospective internal and independent external cohorts bound the diagnostic claim. The result is reported in the Cancer Cell International. It does not establish generalization beyond the reported setting or prospective real-world benefit.
ai_technology: LASSO and random-forest feature selection plus 11 trained machine-learning models, including a Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT), were used to predict postoperative intracranial infection from cerebrospinal-fluid parameters.
organization: Shandong Cancer Hospital and Institute; Shandong First Medical University; Shandong Academy of Medical Sciences
